initialNavigation.title: Moriarty Webs — A field guide to required proofs

actions.action: Clicked “Inspect the invoice worksheet” from the hero.
actions.observed: The page navigated to #worksheet. A fresh context started with Seller payment 35, Source behavior selected, escrow funding 110, seller receipt 35, fee recipient receipt 2, cash remaining 73, invoice duty 65, reserve duty 10, and total duties 75.
actions.taskOutcome: Helpful: the 35 payment reduces the 100 invoice duty to 65; the separate 10 reserve duty remains, so total duties are 75. The 2 fee does not pay down the invoice. In source mode the resulting 73 CASH is 2 below the 75 duties.
evidence: Supplied worksheet screenshot shows 112 proposed funding, unlike the fresh browser default; see finding F01.

actions.action: Focused Seller payment and used Home then 41 ArrowRight key presses to change it from 35 to 42.
actions.observed: The live values updated to seller receives 42, fee recipient receives 2, cash remaining 66, invoice duty 58, reserve duty 10, total duties 68; source funding stayed 110 and the worksheet displayed a 2 CASH backing gap. Gross escrow debit was 44.
actions.taskOutcome: Helpful: moving the slider makes clear that the fee does not discharge invoice duty, and the remaining duties track the unpaid invoice plus reserve.

actions.observed: For the 42 payment, funding changed to 112, cash remaining became 68, and total duties remained 68. The page says the extra 2 is an assumption beyond source open, S12 has no extra-funding action, and later partials need another fee allowance.
actions.taskOutcome: Helpful: I understand 112 as a proposed one-partial funding policy that adds 2 to cover the partial fee; it is not what the source action does.

actions.action: Opened “Exact asset, opening costs & lifecycle limits.”
actions.observed: The disclosure says CASH is the S12 fixture asset and not a Cardano asset; source open transfers 110 and charges a separate 3 CASH opening fee, for gross buyer debit 113. It also says the reserve duty remains and Close stays blocked under the proposed 112 policy, and later partials need more fee allowance.
actions.taskOutcome: Helpful for understanding the separate opening fee and why the reserve survives; this detail is below the worksheet and must be opened.

actions.action: Opened the page question “Can S12 fund the escrow with 112?”
actions.observed: The answer says 112 is a proposed application policy; S12 open funds face plus reserve and has no extra transfer, and only non-negative custody is enforced.
actions.taskOutcome: Helpful: directly answered whether the 112 amount is an existing source action (it is not).
evidence: Visible FAQ answer “Can S12 fund the escrow with 112?”

actions.action: Clicked “Explore a Web” and read the A Web and A Strand explanations; opened “What is a Strand?” and “Does restoring a Strand verify the Web?”
actions.observed: The page calls a Web a proposed script-bound collection of Strands required by a consuming contract for one transition. A Strand is an individual proof with its claim, statement, and binding metadata. The FAQ says illustrated roles are not proof verification, acceptance, or settlement.
actions.taskOutcome: Helpful for my teach-back: it defines the terms while clearly marking this site’s examples as illustrations.
evidence: FAQ answers “What is a Strand?” and “Does restoring a Strand verify the Web?”

capturedAfter: Exact asset, opening costs & lifecycle limits opened
